Order
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order, dated 26.07.2022, (Annexure P-1) whereby punishment of recovery of Rs.4,82,423/- has been imposed upon the petitioner. He has been also imposed with the punishment of censure. 2. The petitioner, during the period from 29.09.2015 to 30.11.2020, was posted as Range Assistant in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia. In relation to certain illegal excavation of the minerals, a charge-sheet under Rule 16 of The Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966 was issued to the petitioner on 28.11.2020 (Annexure P-3). The petitioner gave detailed reply to this charge-sheet on 21.10.2021 (Annexure P-4) and, thereafter, the respondents have passed the impugned order on 25.07.2022, whereby the petitioner was found guilty of dereliction of duty, as a result of which loss of Rs.4,82,423/- was caused to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 2 WP-19351-2022 Government, which has been directed to be recovered from the petitioner. In relation to certain illegal excavation of the minerals, a charge- sheet under Rule 16 of The M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966 was issued to the petitioner on 28.11.2020 (Annexure P-3). The petitioner gave detailed reply to this charge-sheet on 21.10.2021 (Annexure P-4) and, thereafter, the respondents have passed the impugned order on 25.07.2022, whereby the petitioner was found guilty of dereliction of duty, as a result of which loss of Rs.4,82,423/- was caused to the Government, which has been directed to be recovered from the petitioner. He was also censured. Challenging this order, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner challenged the impugned order of punishment on two grounds. Firstly, he submitted that since the petitioner raised disputed question of facts in his reply, a detailed departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted by the respondents under Rule 14 of CCA Rules. Secondly, he submitted that since the petitioner had already retired on 30.09.2020, the punishment order could not have been passed without the approval of the Governor. The learned counsel for the petitioner also challenged the finding recorded against him in the impugned order on merits. He, therefore, prays for setting aside the impugned order. Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of O.K. Bharadwaj Vs. Union of India & Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30314626/ 1 others reported in (2001)9 SCC 180. 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that admittedly during the period from 29.09.2015 to 30.11.2020, the petitioner was posted as Range Assistant in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia, wherein illegal excavation of minerals were found. He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount to the loss caused to the Government. He further submits that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner. Learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his submission has placed reliance upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case o f O.K. Bharadwaj (supra). However, the judgment passed in the said case was considered and explained by this Court in the case of Roop Singh Bhadouria Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P.No.7788/2011) . After considering various judgments including the judgment of O.K. Bharadwaj (Supra), this Court held that while imposing minor punishment, a detailed enquiry is not required to be conducted in every case. This Court has held in para 17 & 18 as under : "17. Division Bench of this Court in the case of Ratan Singh Silawat (supra) has held in similar lines as held in the case of C.P. Singh (supra). However, said discretion is to be exercised reasonably and objectively and it should not be guided by the arbitrariness." 7. 8. The learned counsel for the petitioner tried to assail the finding recorded by the authority on merits of the case. Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of O.K. Bharadwaj Vs. Union of India & others reported in (2001)9 SCC 180. Secondly, he submitted that since the petitioner had already retired on 30.09.2020, the punishment order could not have been passed without the approval of the Governor in view of provisions of Rule 9 of M.P. Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1976. He, therefore, prayed for setting aside the Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199916415/ 1 impugned order. 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that admittedly during the period from 29.09.2015 to 30.11.2020, the petitioner was posted as Range Assistant in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia, wherein illegal excavation of minerals were found. He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount of loss caused to the Government. He further submitted that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner. Rule 16(1) reads as under:- "1. Subject to the provisions of sub-rule (3) of Rule 15, no order imposing on a Government servant any of the penalties specified in clauses (i) to (iv) of Rule 10 and Rule 11 shall be made except after- (a) informing the Government servant in writing of the proposal to take action against him and of the imputations of misconduct or misbehaviour on which it is proposed to be taken, and giving him a reasonable opportunity of making such representation as he may wish to make against the proposal; (b) holding an inquiry in the manner laid down in sub- rules (3) to (23) of Rule 14, in every case in which the disciplinary authority is of the opinion that such inquiry is necessary; (c) taking the representation, if any, submitted by the Government servant under clause (a) and the record of inquiry, if any, held under clause (b) into consideration; (d) recording a finding on each imputation of misconduct or misbehaviour; and (e) consulting the commission where such consultation is necessary. (1-a) Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (b) of sub-rule (1), if in a case it is proposed after considering the representation, if any, made by the Government Servant under clause (a) of that sub-rule to withhold increments of pay of Stagnation Allowance and such withholding or increments Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199916415/ 2 of pay or Stagnation Allowance is likely to effect adversely the amount of pension payable to the Government Servant or to withhold increments of pay or Stagnation allowance for a period exceeding three years of to withhold increments of pay or Stagnation allowance with cumulative effect for any period, an inquiry shall be held in the manner laid down in sub- rules (3) to (23) of Rule 14, before making any order imposing on the Government servant any such penalty." 8. Thus, under clause (b) of Rule 16(1), the disciplinary authority has been given liberty to form an opinion as to whether enquiry as contemplated under Rule 14 is required in the facts and circumstances of the case or not? 9. Pari materia provisions of Regulation 16 of the Food Corporation of India (Staff) Regulations, 1971 were under considered by the Apex Court in the case of the Food Corporation of India, Hyderabad & others Vs. Prahalada Rao & another reported in (2001)1 SCC 165 wherein the Court held in para 5 as under:- "5. Regulation 60(1)(b) mandates the disciplinary authority to form its opinion whether it is necessary to hold inquiry in a particular case or not. Further, Regulation 60(2) itself provides that in a case if it is proposed to withhold increments of pay and such withholding of increments is likely to affect adversely the amount of retirement benefits payable to an employee and in such other cases as mentioned therein, the disciplinary authority shall hold inquiry in the manner laid down in Regulation 58 before making any order imposing any such penalty. It also erred in holding that where an employee denies that loss is caused to the Corporation either by his negligence or breach of order, such inquiry should be held. As per the Regulation, holding of Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199916415/ 3 regular departmental enquiry is a discretionary power of the disciplinary authority which is to be exercised by considering the facts of each case and if it is misused or used arbitrarily, it would be subject to judicial review." 10. Learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon judgment of the Apex Court in the case of O.K. Bhardwaj (supra) to say that full fledged departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted. The judgments rendered in the case of O.K. Bhardwaj and FCI (supra) have been reconciled by the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Union of India & another Vs. C.P. Singh reported in 2004(2) MPJR 252 (= 2004 SCC Online MP 811). The Court held as under:- "Position after decision in FCI: Where the Rules give a discretion to the Disciplinary Authority to either hold a summary enquiry or regular enquiry, it is not possible to say that the Disciplinary Authority should direct only a regular enquiry, when an employee denies the charge or requests for an inquiry. If he decides not to hold a regular enquiry and proceeds to decide the matter summarily, the employee can always challenge the minor punishment imposed, on the ground that the decision not to hold a regular enquiry was an arbitrary decision. On the other hand, the decision in FCI holding that the Disciplinary Authority has the discretion to dispense with a regular enquiry, even where the charge is factual and the employee denies the charge, is with reference to the specific provisions of a Rule vesting such discretion." 17. Rule 9 of the Pension Rules provides as under: "9. Right of governor to withhold or withdraw pension.-(1) The Governor reserves to himself the right of withholding or withdrawing a pension or part thereof, whether permanently or for a specified period, and of ordering recovery from pension of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Government if, in any departmental or judicial proceeding, the pensioner is found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence during the period of his service, including service rendered upon re- employment after retirement: Provided that the State Public Service Commission shall be con-sulted before any final orders are passed: Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199916415/ 5 Provided further that where a part of pension is withheld or withdrawn, the amount of such pension shall not be reduced below Ithe minimum pension as determined by the Government from time to time: (2) (a) The departmental proceedings 2[x x x), if instituted while the Government servant was in service whether before his retirement or during his re-employment, shall, after the final retirement of the Government servant, be deemed to be proceedings under this rule and shall be continued an concluded by the authority by which they were commenced, in the same manner as if the Government servant had continued in service: Provided that where the departmental proceedings are instituted by an authority subordinate to the Governor, that authority shall submit a report regarding its findings to the Governor."
